review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve conditional passkeys for unidentified users**

The new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` now requires a non-null user. Both `authenticate()` and the error `challenge()` only call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(...)` when this helper returns true. That method is what sets `enableWebAuthnConditionalUI`, which the login templates (e.g. `themes/.../passkeys.ftl`) use to render the passkey/conditional UI. With this change, initial login screens where `context.getUser()` is null will no longer set that attribute, so passkey login/conditional UI is not offered for first-factor authentication, breaking passkey sign-in unless the user is already identified.

prs.title: Add AuthzClientCryptoProvider for authorization client cryptographic operations

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make provider selection deterministic on ties**

When more than one `CryptoProvider` is on the classpath, this now sorts by `order()` and silently picks the first provider. In this commit, `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider`, and `FIPS1402Provider` all return `200`, so the sort does not break ties and `ServiceLoader` iteration order (which is unspecified) decides the winner. In environments where multiple providers are packaged (e.g., a FIPS setup that still ships the default provider), this can select a non-FIPS provider without any error, which is a behavior regression compared to the previous hard-fail. Consider assigning distinct orders or restoring a tie check to avoid non-deterministic crypto backends.

prs.title: Add rolling-updates feature flag and compatibility framework
Add Client resource type and scopes to authorization schema

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use resourceServer clientId for resource lookup**

This lookup passes `server.getId()` as the owner, but `ResourceStore.findByName(resourceServer, name)` defaults to `resourceServer.getClientId()` as the owner and resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema` use that owner. As a result, per-client resources won’t be found, so fine-grained client permissions will be ignored unless an “all-clients” permission exists. This will deny access for admins who only have per-client MANAGE/VIEW/CONFIGURE permissions in V2. Consider using the default `findByName(server, client.getId())` (or `server.getClientId()` as owner) to match the stored owner.

prs.title: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Return actual group IDs for view-members filtering**

`getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is adding `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource UUID), but `UserModel.GROUPS` is later used by `JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery` to match `UserGroupMembershipEntity.groupId`, which stores Keycloak **group IDs**. This mismatch means group-scoped `VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS` permissions won’t surface any users unless an “all-groups” permission exists, because the subquery never matches membership rows. You likely want to add `groupResource.getName()` (or otherwise map back to the group id) instead of the resource id when building the set.

prs.title: Add HTML sanitizer for translated message resources

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read message bundles with UTF-8 to avoid false HTML errors**

The new HTML check builds `PropertyResourceBundle` directly from a `FileInputStream`, which per JDK docs assumes ISO‑8859‑1 encoding. These message `.properties` files are UTF‑8 in this repo, so non‑ASCII translations will be misdecoded (mojibake). That can introduce stray `<`/`>` bytes or alter text such that the sanitizer comparison fails, causing valid translations to be reported as “Illegal HTML” and failing the verifier for some locales. Use an `InputStreamReader` with UTF‑8 (or `ResourceBundle.Control` with UTF‑8) so the HTML check runs on the real message text.

prs.title: Implement access token context encoding framework

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accepts wrong grant in token-id matcher**

The matcher returns `false` when the encoded grant shortcut matches the expected one and returns `true` when it does not, so correct token IDs will fail assertions and incorrect grants can pass. This is visible in the `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` branch; with the encoded layout (sessionType+tokenType+grantType) the grant shortcut should be checked for equality and treated as a match. As written, any valid access token id produced with the expected grant will fail tests that use this matcher.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Null rawTokenId is not validated**

The constructor intends to enforce non-null inputs, but it checks `grantType` twice and never validates `rawTokenId`. This allows `rawTokenId` to be null while still passing validation, which then flows into `encodeTokenId` and creates an invalid token id (e.g., `...:null`) without throwing early. The second `requireNonNull` should guard `rawTokenId` instead.

prs.title: Implement recovery key support for user storage providers
Fix concurrent group access to prevent NullPointerException

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve non-null subgroup count contract**

GroupModel’s contract states that `getSubGroupsCount()` “never returns null” (see server-spi GroupModel javadoc). Returning `null` here when `modelSupplier.get()` is missing breaks that contract and propagates a nullable value into `GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount`, which is treated as a number by admin UI code (e.g., comparisons against `0`). In scenarios where the cache entry is accessed after invalidation and `modelSupplier` yields `null`, this can trigger unexpected UI behavior or downstream NPEs when callers unbox the count. Consider returning `0` or falling back to a safe count instead of `null`.
